item.title: Eagles
item.description:
The Eagles are, without a doubt, my absolute favorite band. Even though their behind-the-scenes relationships were far from perfect - Don Felder even had a bitter legal battle with them, and they fully embraced the wild, reckless chaos of the 70s hippie era, with Don Henley and Glenn Frey often ruling the group with an iron fist, none of that changes how deeply I love their music and style.

It is fascinating how a band living such an untamed, rebellious lifestyle could write such incredibly delicate, meticulous lyrics. Their performances are simply flawless; from every specific tone and pitch to their overall presence, it is all crafted to absolute perfection. Diving deep into their intense, dramatic history has only made me appreciate their artistry even more. They were walking contradictions, but they were absolute musical geniuses, without a single doubt.

item.title: Michael Jackson
item.description: Michael Jackson is one of the artists I return to when I want pop music that feels carefully built around rhythm, movement, drama, and visual storytelling. Honestly, my only regret is that I didn’t dive into his world sooner. It wasn’t until I watched the Broadway show MJ the Musical and his documentary film that I truly fell in love with his artistry and started listening to all of his songs on repeat. He is a 100% absolute genius. Without a single doubt.

item.title: Bob Seger
item.description: There’s a raw, nostalgic power in Bob Seger’s music. “Night Moves” isn’t just a rock song; it’s a cinematic trip back to your teenage years packed into acoustic strumming and a killer groove. It perfectly captures that bittersweet, universal feeling of growing up, looking back, and realizing you didn’t know how good you had it until the time had already passed.

item.title: David Bowie
item.description: There’s a strange, magnetic power in his music. Bowie didn’t just sing songs; he invited us to step into his weird, wonderful universe. He made it perfectly okay to be an alien, reminding us that being different is exactly what makes you legendary, and always make me think that sometimes being different doesn’t mean you are a freak, you are just unique.

item.title: Prince
item.description: There’s a strange, magnetic power in his music. Prince didn’t just sing songs; he invited us to step into his flamboyant, boundary-pushing universe. He shared a similar fearless, rule-breaking energy with Bowie, but served it with a completely different kind of swagger. He made it perfectly okay to blur the lines of gender, genre, and fashion. Whenever critics judged his style or doubted his vision, he didn’t argue or explain himself, instead, he just delivered a top-tier performance that forced everyone to shut up. He was fearless.

item.title: Tracy Chapman
item.description: There’s a quiet power in her music. “Fast Car” isn’t just a song; it’s an entire cinematic journey packed into acoustic strumming. It perfectly captures that universal feeling of wanting to leave your current life behind and just keep driving.

item.title: Queen
item.description: Queen is one of the bands I return to when I want music that feels larger than the room.
